newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Purneftegaz will not pay 1996 dividends. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Russian Purneftegaz will not pay 1996 dividends. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: Russian oil holding company Rosneft said on Monday production unit Purneftegaz would not pay dividends on 1996 earnings and would increase capital by 6.4 trillion roubles from 4.45 billion roubles
Purneftegaz paid 1995 dividends of 793 roubles on preferred shares with a face value of 40 roubles but did not pay dividends on ordinaries.

A Rosneft spokesman said the company was creating authorised but unissued capital of 6.4 trillion roubles comprising 4.8 billion (corrects from million) ordinary shares and 1.6 billion (corrects from million) preferred shares with a face value of 1,000 roubles.
He said capital would be increased by revaluing the company's assets. It is not uncommon for Russian companies to raise capital 1,000-fold.
Additional shares will be divided among existing shareholders in proportion to their current stake, the Rosneft spokesman said.
He did not say when the share issue would take place.
Marksmir Kim, first vice-president of Purneftegaz's main shareholder Rosneft, was elected chairman to replace Viktor Ageyev. Rosneft owns 38 percent of Purneftegaz shares.
Purneftegaz has previously said that its pre-tax profit calculated to Russian standards on an accruals basis was 592.02 billion roubles in 1996, up from 310.07 billion roubles in 1995.
